papers.title: A Goal Without a Plan Is Just a Wish: Efficient and Effective Global Planner Training for Long-Horizon Agent Task
papers.abstract: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) struggle with brainless trial-and-error and generating hallucinatory actions due to a lack of global planning in long-horizon tasks. In this paper, we introduce a plan-and-execute framework and propose EAGLET, an efficient and effective planner training method to enhance the executor agent's planning abilities without human effort. Specifically, we train a plug-and-play global planner through a two-step process: we first synthesize high-quality plans from an advanced LLM using our proposed homologous consensus filtering strategy, and apply fine-tuning as a cold start. Moreover, we further improve the planner with a rule-based reinforcement learning stage using a novel executor capability gain reward, ensuring it can handle task instructions of varying difficulty. Experiments on three long-horizon agent tasks show that executor agents equipped with our planner outperform existing methods, achieving new state-of-the-art performance. Meanwhile, EAGLET reduces training costs by 8× compared to RL-based baselines, and it does not require manual effort or extra training data, offering an efficient and effective solution.

summary.method: 通过共识过滤的计划合成和基于规则的强化学习（使用能力提升奖励），训练即插即用的全局规划器。
summary.takeaway: EAGLET 高效训练全局规划器，提升 LLM 代理的长时程表现，无需人工数据。
summary.problem: LLM 代理缺乏全局规划，导致长时程任务中反复试错和幻觉行为。
summary.evidence: 配备该规划器的执行代理在三项任务上达到 state‑of‑the‑art 结果，训练成本比 RL 基线降低 8 倍。
summary.why_for_you: 如果您需要高效、无需对抗训练的方式提升 LLM 在长时程任务中的规划能力，则本研究相关。
summary.limitations: 论文未提供量化性能数据或计划质量分析。

experiments.title: 三项长时程代理任务的评估

mechanism.detail: 共识过滤在多个 LLM 输出中挑选一致的计划片段，确保规划器从可靠轨迹开始训练。

open_questions: EAGLET 在更复杂或真实环境中的可扩展性如何？
该方法对 LLM 代理对抗鲁棒性的影响如何？

deep_dive.overview: 本文针对 LLM 代理缺乏全局规划的问题，提出名为 EAGLET 的计划‑执行框架。首先通过同源共识过滤的高质量计划合成，对即插即用的全局规划器进行冷启动。随后在基于规则的强化学习阶段，以执行器能力提升为奖励对规划器进行微调。三项长时程任务的实验显示，方法达到 state‑of‑the‑art 性能，训练成本比 RL 基线降低八倍，且无需人工数据收集。

papers.title: POET-X: Memory-efficient LLM Training by Scaling Orthogonal Transformation
papers.abstract: Efficient and stable training of large language models (LLMs) remains a core challenge in modern machine learning systems. To address this challenge, Reparameterized Orthogonal Equivalence Training (POET), a spectrum-preserving framework that optimizes each weight matrix through orthogonal equivalence transformation, has been proposed. Although POET provides strong training stability, its original implementation incurs high memory consumption and computational overhead due to intensive matrix multiplications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce POET-X, a scalable and memory-efficient variant that performs orthogonal equivalence transformations with significantly reduced computational cost. POET-X maintains the generalization and stability benefits of POET while achieving substantial improvements in throughput and memory efficiency. In our experiments, POET-X enables the pretraining of billion-parameter LLMs on a single Nvidia H100 GPU, and in contrast, standard optimizers such as AdamW run out of memory under the same settings.

summary.method: POET‑X 重新设计正交等价变换，以降低矩阵乘法开销，同时保持 POET 的稳定性优势。
summary.takeaway: POET‑X 提供内存高效的正交等价训练方法，使得在单个 H100 GPU 上预训练十亿参数 LLM 成为可能。
summary.problem: 标准正交等价训练 (POET) 需要大量内存和计算，限制了大规模 LLM 训练。
summary.evidence: POET‑X 成功在一块 Nvidia H100 上训练十亿参数 LLM，而 AdamW 会出现内存不足。
summary.why_for_you: 通过降低大模型的内存和计算需求，契合您对高效 adversarial 训练的兴趣。

experiments.title: 单卡 H100 上的十亿参数 LLM 预训练

findings.title: 内存效率使原本不可行的训练成为可能
findings.detail: POET‑X 降低的内存消耗使得在单 GPU 上成功训练十亿参数 LLM 成为可能，展示出相较于 AdamW 的显著吞吐量和内存提升。

mechanism.title: 保持谱的重新参数化
mechanism.detail: 该方法在更新过程中保持每个权重矩阵的特征值谱，因而据称提供与原始 POET 方法相当的训练稳定性。

open_questions: POET‑X 相较于基线优化器在收敛速度和最终模型质量上有何影响？
降低矩阵乘法与变换中潜在近似误差之间的权衡是什么？
deep_dive.overview: 本文提出 POET‑X——可扩展的 Reparameterized Orthogonal Equivalence Training (POET) 变体，旨在降低正交变换的内存和计算负担。通过重新设计以避免高强度矩阵乘法，POET‑X 保持 POET 的谱保持稳定性，同时实现更高吞吐量和更低内存占用。实验表明，POET‑X 能在单块 Nvidia H100 GPU 上预训练十亿参数语言模型，而传统优化器如 AdamW 会超出内存限制。

papers.title: Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are pre-trained on large data from different sources and domains. These datasets often contain trillions of tokens, including large portions of copyrighted or proprietary content, which raises questions about the legal use of such models. This underscores the need for truly open pre-training data that complies with data security regulations. In this paper, we introduce Common Corpus, the largest open dataset for LLM pre-training. The data assembled in Common Corpus are either uncopyrighted or under permissive licenses and amount to about two trillion tokens. The dataset contains a wide variety of languages, ranging from the high-resource European languages to some low-resource languages rarely represented in pre-training datasets. In addition, it includes a large amount of code data. The diversity of data sources in terms of covered domains and time periods opens up the paths for both research and entrepreneurial needs in diverse areas of knowledge. In this paper, we present the detailed provenance of data assembling and the details of dataset filtering and curation. We train two small language models on Common Corpus and find that they perform comparably to other models of their size, indicating that our dataset is suitable for multilingual pretraining. Common Corpus represents a key contribution to the ecosystem for open science research on Large Language Models.

summary.evidence: 训练的两个小型模型表现与同类模型相当，表明数据集适合多语言预训练。
summary.limitations: 未在摘要中提及具体限制。
summary.method: 收集无版权或宽松许可的数据，进行过滤和整理，并训练小型模型验证效果。
summary.problem: 现有LLM预训练数据常包含版权内容，引发法律使用问题，需真正开放且合规的数据。
summary.takeaway: 提出Common Corpus，最大的开放数据集用于LLM预训练，包含符合数据安全法规的伦理数据。

papers.title: Understanding and Mitigating Bias Inheritance in LLM-based Data Augmentation on Downstream Tasks
papers.abstract: Generating synthetic datasets via large language models (LLMs) has emerged as a promising approach to improve LLM performance. However, LLMs inherently reflect biases in their training data, leading to a critical challenge: when models are trained on synthetic data, they may propagate and amplify the inherent biases that can significantly impact fairness and robustness on downstream tasks—a phenomenon we term bias inheritance. This work presents the first systematic investigation in understanding, analyzing, and mitigating bias inheritance. We fine-tune LLMs with a combined dataset of real and LLM-augmented data with varied bias ratio as the proportion of augmented data. Through systematic experiments across 10 classification and generation tasks, we analyze how 6 different types of biases manifest. Our results indicate that bias inheritance harms downstream task performance in bias directly-related classification and generation tasks. Then, our analysis identifies three key misalignment factors: misalignment of values, group data, and data distributions. Based on these insights, we propose three mitigation strategies: token-based, mask-based, and loss-based approaches, which can work differently on various tasks and bias, indicating the substantial challenges to mitigate bias inheritance. We hope this work can provide insights to the research of LLM data augmentation.

summary.takeaway: LLM 生成的合成数据中的偏见可能被继承并放大，损害下游公平性，且缓解并非易事。
summary.evidence: 在 10 项分类和生成任务上的实验表明，偏见继承会降低偏见相关任务的性能。
summary.limitations: 缓解策略在不同任务和偏见上的效果差异显著，表明面临巨大挑战。
summary.method: 在混合真实与合成数据、不同偏见比例下微调 LLM，并评估基于 token、mask 和 loss 的缓解策略。
summary.why_for_you: 对研究数据选择和可信 LLM 有重要意义，因为它揭示了合成增强中的偏见风险。
summary.problem: LLM 增强的训练数据将固有偏见传播至下游任务（偏见继承）。

signals.text: 首次系统性研究 LLM 数据增强中偏见继承，覆盖 10 项任务和 6 类偏见。
提出基于 token、mask 和 loss 的缓解方法，以解决偏见错位。
研究发现偏见继承损害下游性能，但缓解效果因任务和偏见而异。

deep_dive.overview: 本文研究了大型语言模型生成的合成数据如何继承并放大训练数据偏见（称为偏见继承）。通过在真实与 LLM 增强数据的混合数据集上进行微调并控制偏见比例，作者在十个分类和生成基准上考察了六类偏见。文中指出三种错位因素——价值观、群体数据和数据分布——并提出三种缓解策略（基于 token、mask、loss）。结果显示偏见相关任务性能下降，且缓解效果差异显著，凸显彻底解决偏见继承的难度。

methodology.title: Bias‑ratio 控制的微调
methodology.detail: 在真实与合成数据的混合上对 LLM 进行微调，改变增强数据（bias ratio）的比例，以研究其对下游性能的影响。

methodology.title: 缓解策略设计
methodology.detail: 提出三种方法：基于 token 的（调整 token 表示）、基于 mask 的（修改注意力掩码）和基于 loss 的（改变损失函数），用于抵消已识别的错位。

mechanism.title: 错位因素
mechanism.detail: 偏差继承源于真实与合成语料库之间在价值观、群体数据和整体数据分布上的错位。

mechanism.title: 缓解机制
mechanism.detail: 基于 token 的方法旨在重新加权有偏 token，基于 mask 的方法限制有偏注意力模式，基于 loss 的方法在训练中惩罚有偏预测。

experiments.title: 任务套件与偏差分类法
experiments.detail: 评估了十个 classification 和 generation 任务，涵盖六种不同的 bias 类型；系统性地改变 bias ratios，以观察 inheritance effects。

experiments.title: mitigation 评估
experiments.detail: 在任务套件中应用每种 mitigation 策略，测量 downstream performance 的变化，以评估其在各 bias 和任务上的有效性。

findings.title: Bias inheritance 降低性能
findings.detail: 在与 bias 直接相关的 classification 和 generation 任务中，较高的 synthetic bias ratios 导致 downstream accuracy 和 fairness metrics 可测量的下降。

findings.title: 异构 mitigation 结果
findings.detail: Token‑、mask‑、和 loss‑based 方法在部分 bias‑task 组合上提升 performance，但在其他组合上失效或出现回退，凸显 task‑specific 挑战。

contributions: 系统性研究 LLM 生成的合成数据中的偏差继承。
识别导致偏差传播的三个关键错位因素。
提出三种缓解策略（基于 token、基于 mask、基于 loss）。
limitations: 缓解策略在不同任务和偏差类型上的效果差异显著，表明普遍解决偏差继承面临重大挑战。

papers.title: User Perceptions vs. Proxy LLM Judges: Privacy and Helpfulness in LLM Responses to Privacy-Sensitive Scenarios
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly being adopted for tasks like drafting emails, summarizing meetings, and answering health questions. In these settings, users may need to share private information (e.g., contact details, health records). To evaluate LLMs' ability to identify and redact such information, prior work introduced real-life, scenario-based benchmarks (e.g., ConfAIde, PrivacyLens) and found that LLMs can leak private information in complex scenarios. However, these evaluations relied on proxy LLMs to judge the helpfulness and privacy-preservation quality of LLM responses, rather than directly measuring users' perceptions. To understand how users perceive the helpfulness and privacy-preservation quality of LLM responses to privacy-sensitive scenarios, we conducted a user study ($n=94$) using 90 PrivacyLens scenarios. We found that users had low agreement with each other when evaluating identical LLM responses. In contrast, five proxy LLMs reached high agreement, yet each proxy LLM had low correlation with users' evaluations. These results indicate that proxy LLMs cannot accurately estimate users' wide range of perceptions of utility and privacy in privacy-sensitive scenarios. We discuss the need for more user-centered studies to measure LLMs' ability to help users while preserving privacy, and for improving alignment between LLMs and users in estimating perceived privacy and utility.

summary.takeaway: 代理 LLM 评审无法预测用户在隐私敏感情境下对隐私和有用性的感知。
summary.evidence: 用户间评审一致性低，而五个代理 LLM 的一致性高，但与用户评分相关性低。
summary.limitations: 缺乏对 90 PrivacyLens 场景之外的泛化证据。
summary.method: 对 94 名参与者进行的用户研究，评估 90 个 PrivacyLens 场景下 LLM 响应的隐私性和实用性。
summary.why_for_you: 对可信 LLM 研究重要，因为它揭示了基于模型的代理与人类隐私判断之间的不一致。
summary.problem: 当前评估依赖代理 LLM，而非直接测量用户对隐私保护 LLM 行为的判断。

deep_dive.overview: 本文探讨代理 LLM 评审能否替代人类对 LLM 生成响应的隐私和实用性评估。通过招募 94 名参与者对 90 个真实 PrivacyLens 场景的响应进行评分，作者测量用户间的一致性并与五个代理 LLM 的共识比较。结果显示人类意见分歧显著，代理模型内部一致却与人类判断偏离，凸显当前评估实践的缺口并推动以用户为中心的评估方法。
open_questions: 如何设计评估指标以捕捉用户对隐私感知的广泛差异？
哪些方法能使代理 LLM 判断与隐私敏感情境下多样的人类判断保持一致？
limitations: 缺乏对 90 PrivacyLens 场景之外的泛化证据。

signals.text: 代理 LLM 评审在 90 个 PrivacyLens 场景（94 名用户）中对隐私和有用性的人工判断预测效果差。
进行用户研究，对 LLM 响应的隐私和实用性进行评分，并将用户间一致性与五个代理 LLM 进行比较。
用户一致性低（低的 inter‑rater 相关），而代理 LLM 一致性高但与用户相关性低。

methodology.detail: 94 名参与者分别评估 90 个 PrivacyLens 场景下的 LLM 响应，给出对隐私保护和有用性的感知评分。

experiments.detail: 五个代理 LLM 对相同响应生成判断；计算了代理之间的一致性以及与人类评分的相关性。

findings.title: Low Human Agreement

findings.detail: 代理 LLM 达到高内部一致性，但与人类评估的相关性低。

papers.title: OPUS: Towards Efficient and Principled Data Selection in Large Language Model Pre-training in Every Iteration
papers.abstract: As high-quality public text approaches exhaustion, a phenomenon known as the Data Wall—LLM pre-training is shifting from more tokens to better tokens. However, existing methods either rely on heuristic static filters that ignore training dynamics, or use dynamic yet optimizer-agnostic criteria based on raw gradients. We propose OPUS (Optimizer-induced Projected Utility Selection), a dynamic framework that defines utility in the optimizer-induced update space. OPUS scores candidates by projecting their effective updates, shaped by modern optimizers, onto a target direction derived from a stable, in-distribution proxy. To ensure scalability, we employ Ghost technique with CountSketch for computational efficiency, and Boltzmann sampling for data diversity, incurring only 4.7% additional compute overhead. OPUS achieves remarkable results across diverse corpora, quality tiers, optimizers, and model scales. It also outperforms previous data selection methods across different stages of training, including from-scratch pre-training and also mid-training. Beyond online selection, the OPUS utility score also demonstrates potential as a static filter for flagging and removing toxic documents from contaminated training corpora prior to training.

summary.takeaway: OPUS 通过将 optimizer‑induced 更新投影到 target direction，高效选择更高效用的训练标记。
summary.evidence: OPUS 在语料库、optimizers 和模型规模上均优于已有 data‑selection 方法，且仅增加 4.7% 的计算开销。
summary.method: OPUS 通过使用 Ghost、CountSketch 和 Boltzmann 采样，将现代优化器塑造的有效更新投影到由稳定分布代理得到的方向上，为每个候选项打分。
summary.why_for_you: 如果您需要利用训练动态和 optimizer 行为的 data‑selection 方法以实现高效 LLM pre‑training，则本研究相关。
summary.problem: Data Wall 限制了 LLM pre‑training，因为高质量公共文本已枯竭，且现有过滤器忽视训练动态或对 optimizer‑agnostic 不敏感。

signals.text: OPUS 引入了动态、optimizer‑aware 的数据选择框架，通过投影效用为训练样本打分。
OPUS 使用 Ghost 技术结合 CountSketch 与 Boltzmann 采样，将 optimizer‑shaped 的有效更新投影到 target direction。
OPUS 仅增加 4.7% 的计算开销，却在语料库、optimizers 和模型规模上实现更佳性能。

deep_dive.overview: OPUS 通过在 optimizer‑induced 更新空间定义效用来应对 Data Wall。它利用现代优化器计算的有效更新，将其投影到由稳定分布代理得到的 target direction 上，为每个候选标记计算效用分数。通过 Ghost 技术结合 CountSketch 实现可扩展性，并使用 Boltzmann 采样保持数据多样性。跨不同语料库、质量层级、optimizers 和模型规模的实验表明，相比现有静态和动态选择方法，OPUS 能持续提升性能，且仅带来约 4.7% 的计算增量。该效用分数亦可用作有害数据的静态过滤器。

methodology.title: Utility Scoring via Projection
methodology.detail: 每个候选的有效更新（由 optimizer 产生）被投影到反映稳定分布内 proxy 的目标方向上，得到标量效用分数。

methodology.title: 可扩展计算
methodology.detail: Ghost 技术结合 CountSketch 高效近似投影，实现每次迭代评分而不会产生过大开销。

methodology.title: 通过 Boltzmann 采样实现多样性
methodology.detail: 效用分数通过 Boltzmann 分布转化为选择概率，既保证数据多样性，又倾向于高效用样本。

mechanism.title: 优化器诱导的更新空间
mechanism.detail: 现代优化器（如 Adam）生成的更新定义了一个向量空间；OPUS 利用该空间捕获原始梯度方法中缺失的训练动态。

mechanism.title: 来自稳定代理的目标方向
mechanism.detail: 稳定的分布内数据集提供参考方向；将更新投影到该方向上可衡量与期望学习信号的对齐程度。

experiments.title: 实证评估
experiments.detail: 在多个覆盖不同质量层级的语料库上评估 OPUS，使用多种优化器和模型规模，涵盖从头 pre‑training 和 mid‑training 阶段；并与之前的 static filters 和 dynamic gradient‑based selectors 进行比较。

findings.title: 性能提升
findings.detail: 在所有设置下，OPUS 始终优于以往 data selection methods，展示了对语料类型、优化器选择和模型规模的鲁棒性。

findings.title: 计算效率
findings.detail: OPUS 额外的计算成本限制在每次 training iteration 的 4.7%。

findings.title: 静态过滤能力
findings.detail: OPUS utility score 可 offline 用于标记并在 training 前移除 toxic documents。

papers.title: Fine-tuning vs. In-context Learning in Large Language Models: A Formal Language Learning Perspective
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) operate in two fundamental learning modes – fine-tuning (FT) and in-context learning (ICL) – raising key questions about which mode yields greater language proficiency and whether they differ in their inductive biases. Prior studies comparing FT and ICL have yielded mixed and inconclusive results due to inconsistent experimental setups. To enable a rigorous comparison, we propose a formal language learning task – offering precise language boundaries, controlled string sampling, and no data contamination – and introduce a discriminative test for language proficiency, where an LLM succeeds if it assigns higher generation probability to in-language strings than to out-of-language strings. Empirically, we find that: (a) FT has greater language proficiency than ICL on in-distribution generalization, but both perform equally well on out-of-distribution generalization. (b) Their inductive biases, measured by the correlation in string generation probabilities, are similar when both modes partially learn the language but diverge at higher proficiency levels. (c) Unlike FT, ICL performance differs substantially across models of varying sizes and families and is sensitive to the token vocabulary of the language. Thus, our work demonstrates the promise of formal languages as a controlled testbed for evaluating LLMs, behaviors that are difficult to isolate in natural language datasets. Our source code is available at https://github.com/bishwamittra/formallm.

papers.title: Tracing the Roots: A Multi-Agent Framework for Uncovering Data Lineage in Post-Training LLMs
papers.abstract: Post-training data plays a pivotal role in shaping the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet datasets are often treated as isolated artifacts, overlooking the systemic connections that underlie their evolution. To disentangle these complex relationships, we introduce the concept of \textbf{data lineage} to the LLM ecosystem and propose an automated multi-agent framework to reconstruct the evolutionary graph of dataset development. Through large-scale lineage analysis, we characterize domain-specific structural patterns, such as vertical refinement in Math-oriented datasets and horizontal aggregation in General-domain corpora. Moreover, we uncover pervasive systemic issues, including \textit{structural redundancy} induced by implicit dataset intersections and the \textit{propagation of benchmark contamination} along lineage paths. To demonstrate the practical value of lineage analysis for data construction, we leverage the reconstructed lineage graph to create a \textit{lineage-aware diversity-oriented dataset}. By anchoring instruction sampling at upstream leaf sources, this approach mitigates downstream homogenization and hidden redundancy, yielding a more diverse post-training corpus. We further highlight lineage-centric analysis as an efficient and robust topological alternative to sample-level dataset comparison for large-scale data ecosystems. By grounding data construction in explicit lineage structures, our work advances post-training data curation toward a more systematic and controllable paradigm.

papers.title: Jailbreak to Protect: Buffering Harmful Fine-Tuning via Temporary Jailbreaking LoRA in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning-as-a-Service (FaaS) enables personalization of large language models (LLMs) but poses significant safety risks, as fine-tuning user-provided data degrades the model's safety-alignment. Prior works addressing this issue typically rely on explicit regularization, which leads to practical limitations. In this paper, we propose a different paradigm that neutralizes harmful updates via harmful gradient saturation rather than explicit suppression. Our key observation is that, in a jailbroken LLM, safety-degrading gradients are largely saturated, while gradients unrelated to safety remain active during fine-tuning. Based on this insight, we introduce a **BufferLoRA-based fine-tuning framework**. BufferLoRA is a removable adapter that temporarily jailbreaks the model during user fine-tuning, saturating harmful updates while allowing a UserLoRA to learn user-specific tasks. After fine-tuning, BufferLoRA is removed to restore the base model’s original safety-alignment. To further reinforce safety, we additionally train a SafetyLoRA and integrate its safety components into the UserLoRA via QR decomposition-based merging strategy. Extensive experiments show that our framework achieves superior performance in both safety and utility, without requiring additional safety data during fine-tuning and with minimal computational cost.

summary.takeaway: In this paper, we propose a different paradigm that neutralizes harmful updates via harmful gradient saturation rather than explicit suppression.

papers.title: Mechanistic Data Attribution: Tracing the Training Origins of Interpretable LLM Units
papers.abstract: While mechanistic interpretability has identified interpretable circuits in large language models (LLMs), their causal origins in training data remain elusive. We introduce *mechanistic data attribution* (MDA), a scalable framework that employs influence functions to trace interpretable units back to specific training samples. Through extensive experiments on the Pythia family, we causally validate that targeted intervention—removing or augmenting a small fraction of high-influence samples—significantly modulates the emergence of interpretable heads, whereas random interventions show no effect. Our analysis reveals that repetitive structural data (e.g., LaTeX, XML) acts as a mechanistic catalyst. Furthermore, we observe that interventions targeting induction head formation induce a concurrent change in the model’s in-context learning (ICL) capability. This provides direct causal evidence for the long-standing hypothesis regarding the functional link between induction heads and ICL. Finally, we propose a mechanistic data augmentation pipeline that consistently accelerates circuit convergence across model scales, providing a principled methodology for steering the developmental trajectories of LLMs.

summary.takeaway: We introduce *mechanistic data attribution* (MDA), a scalable framework that employs influence functions to trace interpretable units back to specific training samples.

papers.title: Writing-RL: Advancing Long-form Writing via Adaptive Curriculum Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled strong performance in long-form writing, but current training paradigms remain limited: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) remains constrained by data saturation and performance ceilings, while Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Reward (RLVR), though successful in verifiable domains like math and code, cannot be directly migrated to open-ended long-form writing due to a lack of ground-truths. To further advance long-form writing, we present Writing-RL: an Adaptive Curriculum Reinforcement Learning framework to advance long-form writing capabilities beyond SFT. The framework consists of three key components: Margin-aware Data Selection strategy that prioritizes samples with high learning potential, Pairwise Comparison Reward mechanism that provides discriminative learning signals in the absence of verifiable rewards, and Dynamic Reference Scheduling approach, which plays a critical role by adaptively adjusting task difficulty based on evolving model performance. Experiments on 7B-scale writer models show that Writing-RL effectively improves long-form writing performance over strong SFT baselines. Furthermore, we observe that models trained with long-output RL generalize surprisingly well to long-input reasoning tasks, potentially offering a promising perspective for rethinking long-context training.

papers.title: When Do Supervised UQ Ensembles Improve LLM Hallucination Detection? A Robustness Study
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods are widely used for hallucination detection in large language models (LLMs) in closed-book settings where ground-truth evidence is unavailable at inference time. Prior work has proposed combining UQ signals via learned ensembles, but empirical investigations into the robustness of these ensembles are limited. We study a supervised ensembling framework that trains a classifier over heterogeneous UQ-based scorer outputs on a small, domain-specific dataset of labeled LLM responses, then applies it to out-of-sample hallucination classification without retrieval, tools, or reference documents. Across four LLMs, nine datasets, and three generation regimes (short-form QA, long-form generation, and code generation), we provide a systematic robustness analysis along three axes: sample efficiency, in-domain dataset transfer, and generation regime dependence. We find that supervised ensembles outperform the best individual scorer in 30 of 32 settings, with gains realized from as few as 100 labeled instances. Ensembles retain most of their advantage in cases of in-domain transfer under distribution shift, outperforming the best non-ensemble scorer in 23 of 28 transfer settings. Sampling-based black-box ensembles are nearly as effective as full ensembles, while single-generation white-box ensembles offer limited benefit.

summary.takeaway: Supervised ensembles of heterogeneous UQ scorers consistently improve hallucination detection over the best single scorer, even with as few as 100 labeled examples.
summary.problem: Detecting hallucinations in closed‑book LLM outputs without retrieval or reference documents.
summary.method: Train a classifier on a vector of black‑box, white‑box, and reflexive UQ scores from a small domain‑specific labeled set and apply it to out‑of‑sample responses.
summary.evidence: Ensembles outperform the top individual scorer in 30 of 32 settings by AUROC and retain advantage in 23 of 28 distribution‑shift transfer cases.
summary.limitations: Study is limited to four closed‑source LLMs, two factoid long‑form domains, Python code, and does not evaluate cross‑domain or open‑weight model scorers.
summary.why_for_you: Matches your interest in trustworthy LLMs by providing a sample‑efficient, robust hallucination detector.

deep_dive.overview: The paper investigates a supervised ensembling framework that learns to combine diverse uncertainty quantification (UQ) signals for hallucination detection in closed‑book LLM generation. By training simple classifiers on vectors of black‑box, white‑box, and reflexive scorer outputs, the authors evaluate sample efficiency, in‑domain transfer under distribution shift, and generation‑regime dependence across four LLMs, nine datasets, and three output formats. Results show ensembles dominate individual scorers in most settings, with modest labeled data requirements, while black‑box‑only ensembles approach full‑ensemble performance. Limitations include a narrow model and task scope.

methodology.title: Supervised ensemble training
methodology.detail: A classifier (logistic regression, random forest, or gradient boosting) is trained on K‑dimensional vectors of UQ scores s1(y)…sK(y) ∈ [0,1]K derived from heterogeneous scorers; training subsets range from 0.1N to 0.7N of the labeled data.

mechanism.title: Signal combination
mechanism.detail: Supervised learning learns weighted combinations of complementary UQ signals, allowing the model to exploit strengths of black‑box consistency, white‑box token probabilities, and reflexive self‑judgments, thereby improving discrimination between truthful and hallucinated outputs.

experiments.title: Empirical evaluation
experiments.detail: Four LLMs (Gemini‑2.5‑Flash, Gemini‑2.5‑Pro, GPT‑4o, GPT‑4o‑mini) are tested on nine benchmarks covering short‑form math, factual QA, reading comprehension, Python code generation (LiveCodeBench), and long‑form factoid QA (rivers, mushrooms). Metrics include AUROC and expected calibration error (ECE); baselines are the best individual scorer per setting.

findings.title: In‑distribution superiority
findings.detail: With the full training sample (0.7N), ensembles outperform the best individual scorer in 30 of 32 LLM‑dataset settings by AUROC and in 29 of 32 by ECE.

findings.title: Sample efficiency
findings.detail: Performance gains appear with as few as 100 labeled instances, as shown by AUROC curves across training sizes.

findings.title: Transfer robustness
findings.detail: Under in‑domain distribution shift, ensembles remain superior in 23 of 28 transfer settings.

findings.title: Black‑box vs full ensembles
findings.detail: Sampling‑based black‑box ensembles achieve nearly the same AUROC as full ensembles, whereas white‑box‑only ensembles provide limited benefit.

contributions: Systematic robustness analysis of supervised UQ ensembles across sample efficiency, distribution shift, and generation regimes.
limitations: Only four closed‑source LLMs from two providers are evaluated; results may not generalize to open‑weight models.
Long‑form evaluation is limited to two factoid domains and code experiments to Python competitive‑programming tasks.
Cross‑domain, cross‑LLM, and internal‑state scorer combinations are not explored.
open_questions: How do supervised ensembles perform with open‑weight models and internal‑state UQ signals?
Can ensembles trained on one domain or LLM transfer effectively to entirely different domains or other model families?
What is the impact of more diverse long‑form generation tasks (e.g., summarization, multi‑turn dialogue) on ensemble efficacy?
